why: Both analyses narrow Corwin to branded household paper, divest the unrelated acquisitions and surface all three key brutal facts, but Analysis 2 comes closer to the key by stating that the hedgehog fails if the softness gap or cost lead cannot be confirmed, and by naming list-price cuts as doctrine to stop. Analysis 2 is also better calibrated, marking the decline gate as conditional and offering a fallback position, whereas Analysis 1 asserts that the founding formula still works and passes the decline gate despite describing active decline.
